notes: Second labelled pair. Sheets are ref 1260x891 and rev 420x297, exactly 3:1 — but ONLY the sheet furniture maps across that scale. The title block and BOM land bit-on (ref (105,822)/3 = rev (35,273) for the 45/227/16組/0 row), while the drawing area was re-laid out: the `279` dimension sits at ref (215.5,112.6)/3 against rev (203.0,201.1). So position pairs the title block and BOM and proves nothing in the views area; findings there were settled by content and by whole-sheet sweeps instead. TWO DEFECTS FOUND WHILE LABELLING, both recorded here because each would mislead the next annotator. (1) The pinned template for aspect-1.414 has NO `shim` zone at all — its zones are bom/iso/notes/title/title_upper_left/tolerance/views — so the entire シム表 is attributed to `views` and will be compared, against a guideline that says it must never be. The worksheet's own instruction covers this case: if a grouping looks wrong, say so rather than labelling around it. (2) `tools/eval_corpus.py worksheet` renders DIMENSION entities with no position and no zone (`@?` / `—`) because it reads `insert`, and a dimension carries `def_point`. That is how REV-11C appeared out of scope when its def_point (226.9, 86.5) is inside the views polygon — and a dimension is in COMPARABLE_ENTITY_TYPES. CORRECTION, on reading the code after these labels were written: the row was NOT hidden. `triage_row` explicitly refuses to exclude on missing information and routes an anchorless row to `review`, so the safety net held; the defect is that the tool then marked that row with the two symbols the guideline treats as 'ignore'. See the vault note 'Gotcha - The Worksheet Cannot Place a Dimension'. Also noted, not labelled: REV-2DB is not the empty string the worksheet prints, it holds the byte \x82 where the シム表's fifth row label `ｅ` should be — a real corruption in the revision file, inside a safe zone.

A thickness dimension ｔ = 5.0 added on the revision. Established by comparing every dimension on both sides: the reference has five (279, 195, 130, 24, 271) and the revision has those same five plus this one. ⚠ The worksheet shows this row with position `@?` and zone `—`, which reads as out-of-scope, and that is a worksheet defect rather than a zone fact: it resolves position from `insert` and a DIMENSION carries `def_point`. This one's def_point (226.9, 86.5) is inside the views polygon, and a dimension is in COMPARABLE_ENTITY_TYPES, so the engine can and should see it.

An isometric view was added — the same shape as the M7452A0N01 finding and invisible to the worksheet for the same reason: it carries no text. Measured against the pinned aspect-1.414 iso box: the reference's (x 966–1170, y 549–757) holds ONE stray line; the revision's (x 322–390, y 183–252) holds 20 entities — 13 line, 6 ellipse, 1 block — and the reference has no ellipse anywhere on the sheet. BOTH sides hold zero text and zero dimension there, so with COMPARABLE_ENTITY_TYPES = ('text', 'dimension') the engine cannot report this at any setting: a structural false negative, now recorded on a second human pair. Anchored at REV#508, the first ellipse. ⚠ A strict reading of anchor rule 3 would give REV#394 — the lowest payload index inside the box — but that is a BOM rule line bleeding into the region, not part of the view; the rule needs judgement where a box and a view are not the same set.
